title: Boss: refactor a config in vim
summary: Combine operators, :s and :g into one scripted vim session.

steps.title: One file, many edits
steps.body: You will build a small Ex interpreter that runs the commands a vim user would type to clean up a config file: global deletes, substitutions and line moves.

steps.title: :g and :v
steps.prompt: Write `List<string> Global(List<string> lines, string command)` for commands of the form `:g/<text>/d` and `:v/<text>/d` (also `:g!/<text>/d`): delete every line that contains (for `:g`) or does not contain (for `:v` and `:g!`) the plain text `<text>`. As special cases, `<text>` of `^$` means "the line is empty", and a `<text>` starting with `^` means "the line starts with the rest".
hints: Pull the text out between the first and last `/`.
A line is kept when `Matches(line) == invert`.
template: var dojoLog = new List<string> { "INFO start", "ERROR disk", "", "# note", "ERROR net" };
Dojo.Eq(":v keeps errors", new List<string> { "ERROR disk", "ERROR net" }, Global(dojoLog, ":v/ERROR/d"));
Dojo.Eq(":g deletes errors", new List<string> { "INFO start", "", "# note" }, Global(dojoLog, ":g/ERROR/d"));
Dojo.Eq(":g/^$/d removes blank lines", new List<string> { "INFO start", "ERROR disk", "# note", "ERROR net" }, Global(dojoLog, ":g/^$/d"));
Dojo.Eq(":g/^#/d removes comments", new List<string> { "INFO start", "ERROR disk", "", "ERROR net" }, Global(dojoLog, ":g/^#/d"));

steps.title: Run a vim session
prompt: Write `List<string> Run(List<string> lines, string[] commands)` that runs a mix of normal-mode and Ex commands on a buffer. The cursor starts on line 0. Support:
- `"j"`, `"k"`, `"gg"`, `"G"`, and `":<n>"` (go to line n, 1-based), all clamped,
- `"dd"`, `"yy"`, `"p"`, `"P"` as in lesson 1 (one-line register; `p` moves onto the pasted line, `P` too),
- `"<n>dd"` (for example `"3dd"`): delete n lines starting at the cursor into the register (now holding several lines; `p`/`P` paste all of them and put the cursor on the first pasted line),
- substitute commands (anything containing `s/` or `s#` after the range, like `":%s/a/b/g"`) using your rules from lesson 4,
- `":g/<text>/d"` and `":v/<text>/d"` using the rules above; after them the cursor goes to line 0.
Unknown commands are ignored. The helpers `Substitute` and `Global` are yours to write again (or copy).
solution: List<string> Substitute(List<string> lines, int current, string command)
string pattern = parts[0], replacement = parts.Length > 1 ? parts[1] : "", flags = parts.Length > 2 ? parts[2] : "";

for (int r = from; r <= to && r < result.Count; r++)
int at = pattern.Length == 0 ? -1 : line.IndexOf(pattern, i, cmp);
if (at < 0) { sb.Append(line, i, line.Length - i); break; }
if (!global) { sb.Append(line, i, line.Length - i); break; }
int Clamp(int r) => Math.Max(0, Math.Min(r, text.Count - 1));
else if (c.StartsWith(":g") || c.StartsWith(":v")) { text = Global(text, c); row = 0; }
else if (c.StartsWith(":") && (c.Contains("s/") || c.Contains("s#"))) text = Substitute(text, row, c);
else if (c.StartsWith(":") && int.TryParse(c.Substring(1), out var n)) row = Clamp(n - 1);
int count = c == "dd" ? 1 : int.TryParse(c.Substring(0, c.Length - 2), out var k) ? k : 0;
else if (c == "yy") { if (text.Count > 0) register = new List<string> { text[row] }; }
hints: Order your checks: `:g`/`:v` first, then substitutions, then `:<number>`.
For `<n>dd`, use `GetRange` and `RemoveRange`, limiting n to the lines left.
template: var dojoConf = new List<string> { "# app config", "", "host=localhost", "port=80", "", "# logging", "level=debug", "file=/var/log/app.log" };
Dojo.Eq("clean up a config", new List<string> { "host=0.0.0.0", "port=8080", "level=info", "file=/srv/log/app.log" },
Dojo.Eq("move a block of two lines to the end", new List<string> { "c", "d", "a", "b" }, Run(new List<string> { "a", "b", "c", "d" }, new[] { "2dd", "G", "p" }));
Dojo.Eq("duplicate the last line", new List<string> { "a", "b", "b" }, Run(new List<string> { "a", "b" }, new[] { "G", "yy", "p" }));
Dojo.Eq("P pastes above", new List<string> { "b", "a" }, Run(new List<string> { "a", "b" }, new[] { "j", "dd", "gg", "P" }));
Dojo.Eq("count larger than the rest of the file", new List<string> { "a" }, Run(new List<string> { "a", "b", "c" }, new[] { "j", "9dd" }));
Dojo.Eq("unknown commands are ignored", new List<string> { "a" }, Run(new List<string> { "a" }, new[] { "zz", ":wat" }));
